name: Lay smoke
summary: On a key, the unit fills an area with a cloud of smoke for a short time: around itself, where a thrown or fired canister lands, or as a screen across the line of fire. Nobody sees through the cloud, so shooters outside cannot pick targets in or behind it, and units inside see only what is right beside them. It hides both sides alike, so it covers an advance, a retreat, a crossing or a revive, and it can be thrown onto the enemy to blind their guns. It does no damage and stops no bullet: area fire and anything that aims at the ground still hit what hides there. Unlike cloak, it hides an area from everyone rather than one unit from enemies; unlike shroud-area, it is a visible cloud both teams must respect.
counterplay: Fire blind into the cloud with grenades, mortars or other area weapons; they need no line of sight to hit what hides there.
Walk into or round the cloud: units inside see whatever is right beside them, and a short-range fighter wins there.
Wait it out and cover its edges: the cloud is short-lived, so whoever hides in it has to come out somewhere.
Watch for muzzle flashes: in some versions firing from inside gives the shooter away for a moment.

other_examples.note: This Saxon medium mech can wrap itself in a smoke screen; its wiki page describes the cloud as trailing it while it walks. The developers' later change log made smoke screens smaller and shorter in general and made this mech's and the Mocny's screens stay where they were laid instead of moving with the unit.

sources.title: Sd. KS 78 "Isegrim", Iron Harvest Wiki (Fandom)
sources.note: The page text predates the change log below.

other_examples.unit: PM-41 82mm Mortar Squad: Fire Smoke Barrage
other_examples.note: At no cost, the Soviet mortar team drops several smoke shells on a spot at range (not too close to itself), hiding the whole area; it shares its wait with the damaging barrage. Units cannot shoot into or through the cloud, except cannons and flamethrowers ordered to attack the ground, so it covers an advance or a retreat; setting up and shell flight add a delay.

sources.title: PM-41 82mm Mortar Squad, Company of Heroes Wiki (Fandom)

other_examples.note: The heavy tank's defensive special ability launches a volley of smoke grenades so the tank drops out of sight, and then has to recharge; a self-screen used to break contact.

sources.title: M1A1 Abrams, World in Conflict Wiki (Fandom)

other_examples.note: The unarmed Zerg flier spends energy to spit a cloud at range; ground units and structures under it can reach only a tiny distance with their weapons for some seconds (shorter in Legacy of the Void than in Heart of the Swarm), but they can walk out and fire normally again. A campaign version stops all shooting from under it. A blinding variant: the cloud cripples the shooters inside rather than hiding them.

sources.title: Template:SC2BlindingCloud, StarCraft Wiki (Fandom)
sources.version: StarCraft II: Heart of the Swarm and Legacy of the Void

shooter_analogues.note: In this top-down war game, a smoke grenade, thrown or fired from a launcher, makes a small cloud for a short while after a fixed fuse. Players outside cannot see soldiers in or behind it, and players inside see only soldiers right next to them; shooting from in or behind the cloud reveals the shooter briefly. Computer-run defences are not blinded but fire shorter, slower and less accurately through it. Smoke once switched those defences off entirely, was pulled from the game as too strong, and came back with the weaker rule.

sources.title: PT-815 Smoke Grenade, Official Foxhole Wiki
sources.version: returned in update 0.48 with the current rule

shooter_analogues.note: Her tactical ability fires a fast canister further than a grenade can be thrown; it bursts into a short wall of smoke across the line of fire. It has two charges and can be fired while shooting or healing. The smoke hides both teams, so it works best on the enemy or between the teams, and smoking your own revive is a gamble; it also switches off controller aim assist. Enemies answer by throwing grenades into it or using scopes that highlight targets; a later perk lets allies heal inside her smoke.
A rare thrown grenade that bursts into a large, thick cloud on impact for a while, blocking sight through it for machines and players alike; a smaller version also exists.

player_translation.summary: On a key, drop a short-lived cloud of smoke around you or fire it to a spot: nobody can see through it, so teammates can cross open ground, pull back or revive behind it, or you blind an enemy gun line. It hides your side as much as theirs.
as_user: Smoke the open ground before your team crosses it, or behind you when you need to break off a losing fight.
Fire it onto the enemy's guns or a sniper's lane to blind them while your team closes in.
Remember it hides your enemies too: an enemy can walk into your smoke unseen, so do not park inside it.
It does nothing against grenades and mortars, so do not mistake hidden for safe.
as_target: A cloud appears on the ground: you cannot see or aim at anything in or behind it, but you know where it is.
Throw grenades or call area fire into it, or move to watch where its edges open up.
Close in: inside the cloud you see enemies right beside you, so short-range fighters can hunt in it.
teammates: Smoke can hide a revive or a wounded teammate's escape, though it hides enemies closing in just as well.
The smoke-layer screens a vehicle or an assault squad crossing a field of fire.
Bait and trap: a smoked lane may hide a push or nothing at all, and an ambush can wait inside it.
On the enemy team, area weapons and short-range fighters become the answers.
controls: Q: smoke at your position (a self-screen), or tap-aim and release to fire a canister to a spot within reach.
Siege-mode variant: the same key lobs the canister farther while deployed.
No hold or channel: one press, then a wait that ends roughly when the cloud clears.
feedback: From above, the cloud is drawn as a soft, opaque grey patch that hides units in it from enemies outside, with a clear edge so both teams can see its size.
Units inside are drawn only for players right next to them; a brief flash shows a shooter firing out of it, if that rule is used.
A hiss and a pop where the canister lands, heard from off screen.
The minimap shows the cloud as a grey blot for both teams.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS originals smoke only blocks the line of sight of AI units; in a top-down shooter it must also hide players from each other's screens, which needs server-side vision so clients never learn who is inside.

Iron Harvest moved the Mocny's smoke from following the unit to staying where it is laid, and made it smaller and shorter; a player-held smoke that moves with you is a moving invisibility cloak, so the static cloud is the safer base.
Foxhole's history shows smoke that shuts down defences entirely is too strong; let automated defences shoot shorter and less accurately through smoke instead of stopping.
Aim assist and auto-targeting must respect smoke, as in Apex Legends, or the cloud only works against some players.

team_play.notes: Smoke is a gift to teammates: it covers a crossing, a retreat or a revive, and a well-placed cloud blinds an enemy gun line so the team can close. The enemy answers with area fire and short-range fighters. Word-list gap: no team-play hook fits screening teammates from sight (rescue means undoing an enemy effect on a victim, and escort-dependency means a unit that needs a bodyguard), so only bait-and-trap is used here.

notes: Needs line-of-sight tests that clouds can block, for players, bots and auto-targeting, decided on the server so hidden players are never sent to clients outside.
A rule for what units inside the cloud see (only what is right beside them).
An opaque cloud must render clearly from above without hiding the terrain the players outside need to read.
Particle cost: several clouds at once must stay cheap to draw.

Smoke that follows its owner becomes a moving invisibility field; Iron Harvest's Changelog 24 made the Mocny's and Isegrim's screens static, though it gives no reason for that change (it mentions only fixed technical flaws and smaller, shorter screens).
Many smoke-layers on one team can blanket a whole lane and stall every fight.
If smoke also shuts down automated defences it becomes a must-pick; Foxhole weakened it after it did.
A smoke cloud is a familiar sight that players read at once.
Players must learn that smoke hides but does not protect: area fire still hits inside.

variants.name: Self-screen
variants.summary: The base form: pop a cloud at your own position that stays where you laid it, to break contact or cover nearby allies.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Mocny Smokescreen; World in Conflict M1A1 Abrams Smoke screen

variants.name: Lobbed smoke
variants.summary: Fire or throw a canister to a chosen spot within reach, where the cloud forms.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Mocny Smoke Canister (siege mode); Company of Heroes 2 mortar Fire Smoke Barrage; Foxhole and ARC Raiders smoke grenades

variants.name: Smoke wall
variants.summary: The canister bursts into a short wall of clouds across the line of fire instead of one round cloud.

variants.name: Trailing screen
variants.summary: The smoke follows you as you move for its duration, a moving cover for you and those beside you.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Isegrim and Mocny before Changelog 24 made their screens static

adds_strengths.why: The cloud moves with you, so it covers a whole advance or retreat instead of one spot.

variants.name: Blinding cloud
variants.summary: Enemies inside the cloud can fire only a very short distance until they walk out, so it cripples a gun line rather than hiding allies.

adds_strengths.why: Enemy shooters under the cloud lose nearly all their reach until they leave it, breaking a gun line or a defence.

counters.why: Long-range shooters caught under the cloud can reach only a tiny distance, so they must move and lose their position.

variants.name: Healing smoke
variants.summary: Allies standing in your smoke slowly regain health, which makes it a place to recover as well as to hide.

adds_strengths.why: Blocks sight across an area for a short time, so teammates can cross, retreat or revive unseen, or an enemy gun line is blinded.

adds_weaknesses.why: The cloud hides enemies as well as friends and stops nothing that fires at the ground, so it is cover from sight, not from harm.

counters.why: Long-range shooters cannot pick targets in or behind the cloud; Company of Heroes 2 lets nothing fire through it except attack-ground orders.
Reasoned: a marksman needs a clear line of sight to a target, which the cloud takes away.

countered_by.why: Area fire lands in the cloud without needing to see; Apex Legends players throw grenades into smoke.
In Company of Heroes 2 flame units ordered to attack the ground can still fire into the smoke.
Units inside see enemies right beside them (Foxhole), so short-range fighters can hunt in the cloud.

open_questions: Should smoke stay where it is laid (Iron Harvest after Changelog 24) or follow its owner? (Recommended: static by default, trailing only as a spicy variant.)
Should firing from inside the cloud reveal the shooter for a moment, as in Foxhole?
What do automated defences and bots do against smoke: stop firing, or fire shorter and less accurately as in Foxhole?

shooter_fit.reason: Smoke is a staple of shooters (Apex Legends, Foxhole, ARC Raiders): instantly readable, cheap to build on a server with vision rules, and it creates teamwork around crossings, revives and pushes.
